sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The species comprises a medium-sized (formerly I. gibbifrons) and a large (formerly I. bulbifrons) morph; the two were merged on the basis of distribution, ecology and mitochondrial genome sequences. Soldier: a medium- to large-sized species with the finitimus-type enteric valve armature, head length (to the anterior margin of the clypeus) 2.65—3.76 mm, minor curvature of the left mandible 0.14—0.31 mm, i.e. the mandible is more gently curved; head in lateral view markedly domed, the sagitta of the concavity of the upper margin of the head 0.01—0.12 mm, its mean clearly greater than in I. magniplanifrons, but this is shared with I. severus, I. minitabundus and I. ugandensis (the latter three have the fungifaber-type enteric valve). Alate: medium- to large-sized, head width (across the compound eyes) 1.44—1.73 mm; distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth of the left mandible 0.20—0.30 mm, clearly greater than in the other species with the same enteric valve type. Worker: head width 1.11—1.43 mm, among the medium-sized to largest workers. Ecologically, all known specimens come from forest within about 300 km of the Atlantic coast.

note: Adapted from the species-level diagnosis in the revision by Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the original rests mainly on multivariate morphometrics and molecular data, and the measurement abbreviations have been replaced by descriptive Chinese names in line with the definitions of the original table (head length, head width, mandible curvature, concavity of the upper margin of the head); this entry records only the diagnostic characters given in that revision and does not transcribe its morphological description paragraphs item by item.
